Summary: SEAL learns link-prediction heuristics from local enclosing subgraphs using a GNN; the paper supports the approach with theory and experiments across benchmark networks.
Method: SEAL extracts target-link enclosing subgraphs, labels nodes with double-radius node labeling, and uses a graph-level GNN; optional node embeddings and attributes can be concatenated. A gamma-decay theory argues that high-order heuristics can be approximated from local subgraphs.
Evaluation: Eight networks: USAir, NS, PB, Yeast, C.ele, Power, Router, and E.coli. Evaluation uses 10% held-out positive links and an equal number of sampled negative pairs; the paper reports mean AUC and standard deviations across 10 runs, with average precision also reported in an appendix.
Reported Result: The authors report that SEAL generally outperformed heuristic, latent-feature, and embedding baselines, including WLNM; numeric per-dataset scores are not present in the supplied text.
Baselines: Heuristics: CN, Jaccard, preferential attachment, Adamic–Adar, resource allocation, Katz, PageRank, SimRank, and a logistic-regression ensemble; learned structure methods: Weisfeiler–Lehman graph kernel and WLNM; latent methods: matrix factorization, stochastic block model, node2vec, LINE, spectral clustering, and VGAE.
Evaluation Metrics: AUC and average precision (AP); results averaged over 10 runs with standard deviations.

Summary: ELPH and BUDDY approximate salient subgraph structure with neighborhood sketches; benchmark experiments report competitive prediction and substantially improved runtime, though the supplied text omits most score tables.
Method: ELPH propagates HyperLogLog and MinHash sketches to estimate structural features without constructing per-link subgraphs. BUDDY precomputes sketches and diffused node features for scalable MLP prediction.
Evaluation: Benchmarks include Planetoid citation graphs and OGB link-prediction datasets; experiments compare with heuristics, GCN, GraphSAGE, Neo-GNN, SEAL, and NBFNet. Hyperparameters are selected using validation performance.
Reported Result: The paper reports BUDDY as 200–1000× faster than dynamic SEAL on the citation dataset for training and inference. It also reports that ELPH and BUDDY outperform SGNN baselines on many benchmarks; detailed benchmark score values are not included in the supplied text.
Baselines: Common Neighbors, Adamic–Adar, Resource Allocation, GCN, GraphSAGE, Neo-GNN, SEAL, and NBFNet.
Evaluation Metrics: The supplied text identifies predictive benchmark comparisons and training/inference wall time, but does not specify the predictive metric names in the excerpt.

Summary: NCN pools MPNN representations of common neighbors, while NCNC completes missing common-neighbor structure; the paper reports benchmark gains, but the provided text has inconsistent headline score statements.
Method: NCN runs an MPNN once on the input graph and uses structural common-neighbor sets to pool neighbor representations for each candidate pair. NCNC applies common-neighbor completion using predicted edge probabilities before an additional NCN-style prediction.
Evaluation: Seven benchmarks: Cora, Citeseer, PubMed, ogbl-collab, ogbl-ppa, ogbl-citation2, and ogbl-ddi. The paper reports HITS@100, AUC, runtime/memory comparisons, ablations, and results over 10 random seeds.
Reported Result: The text states NCN exceeds baselines on 5/7 datasets and NCNC is top-performing on all datasets, with an average improvement claim over BUDDY. Numerical table values are not reproduced in the supplied text; separate concluding values differ from the earlier headline claims.
Baselines: CN, RA, AA, GCN, GraphSAGE/SAGE, SEAL, NBFNet, Neo-GNN, and BUDDY.
Evaluation Metrics: HITS@100 and AUC; runtime and GPU memory comparisons; ablation analyses; results reported over 10 random seeds.

Summary: A hybrid text-and-citation clustering of 7,401 bioinformatics publications identified nine static clusters and eleven evolving cluster chains; this is a descriptive bibliometric analysis, not a link-prediction method evaluation.
Method: Combines TF-IDF/LSI text similarity and bibliographic-coupling distances using Fisher’s inverse chi-square, applies Ward hierarchical clustering, and matches clusters across time windows to form chains.
Evaluation: Web of Science and MEDLINE records from 1981–2004; seven consecutive time periods. Cluster selection combines dendrogram inspection, mean silhouette curves, and subsample stability analysis.
Reported Result: The study identifies nine static clusters and eleven cluster chains; the authors describe increasing activity in microarray analysis, systems biology/molecular networks, and phylogeny/evolution. It is thematically adjacent but does not evaluate link-prediction algorithms.
Baselines: No link-prediction baselines apply. The paper discusses hybrid clustering against text-only and citation/link-only approaches, and compares hybrid distance integration with linear combination.
Evaluation Metrics: Mean silhouette values/curves and subsample stability assessed using pairwise Jaccard similarity; dendrogram inspection also informs cluster count.

Summary: IECNC combines common-neighbor completion, MPNN-derived node features, and an entropy term; the paper reports improvements on citation and Twitch datasets, although its supplied text contains conflicting metric values.
Method: Constructs logical neighborhood sets (intersection, union, and directional differences), estimates potential common-neighbor probabilities, aggregates MPNN features, and incorporates probability-based information entropy in link scoring.
Evaluation: Cora, Citeseer, PubMed, Twitch_RU, and Twitch_PT are reported. Metrics include HITS@100 and AUC, with comparisons to heuristic and neural baselines and ablation/parameter analyses.
Reported Result: The paper reports HITS@100 values of 94.09% (Cora), 95.34% (Citeseer), 85.72% (PubMed), 62.18% (Twitch_RU), and 56.27% (Twitch_PT), and AUC values for Cora, Citeseer, and Twitch_PT. Elsewhere it gives different Cora/Citeseer HITS@100 values (94.68% and 96.44%), so the discrepancy requires checking against the original results tables.
Baselines: CN, AA, RA, GCN, SAGE, SEAL, NBFNet, Neo-GNN, BUDDY, NCN, and NCNC.
Evaluation Metrics: HITS@100 and AUC; comparisons of completion/activation variants and component ablations; parameter sensitivity is also assessed using HITS@100 and HITS@10 (the supplied text inconsistently labels some figure captions).
